the-wind-will-carry-us-1999.gazette: Kiarostami took his crew to a real Kurdish village and cast the people who lived there, playing versions of themselves on their own ground. The camera holds at a distance and lets scenes run well past the point where a fiction would cut. What the film calls a story is mostly the village continuing.

a-time-for-drunken-horses-2000.gazette: The mountain crossings between Iran and Iraq are a working economy, and Ghobadi filmed in a border village that lives off them, casting the people who do the work. The title names the practice: mules given alcohol to keep moving through the snow. Nobody in the cast was an actor.

beijing-bicycle-2001.gazette: Wang Xiaoshuai filmed on Beijing streets at the turn of the 2000s, while the hutong courtyards in his frames were being cleared block by block. The bicycle belongs to a courier newly arrived from the countryside, one of the migrant workers the city ran on and did not count. Sixth Generation directors worked this way by necessity: real locations, ordinary labor, no studio gloss.
beijing-bicycle-2001.prism: The demolition behind the actors wasn't set dressing, and it didn't pause for the shoot. Whatever the location footage caught is now the only version of those streets that exists.

what-time-is-it-there-2001.gazette: The camera stays put. Tsai films rooms in Taipei as rooms — real apartments, real stairwells, ambient noise where a score would go — and holds each shot for the length of the action rather than the length of a beat. The fiction agrees to run at the same speed as the day it depicts.

the-son-2002.gazette: The Dardennes shoot in the industrial towns around Liège, in real workshops, with a handheld camera that stays close behind the back of a man's neck. Carpentry is filmed as work — measuring, planing, hauling lumber — and the drama arrives inside it rather than on top of it. No score cues the turn.

unknown-pleasures-2002.gazette: Jia Zhangke took a digital camera to Datong, a declining coal city in Shanxi, and cast people who were already there. On the radios and televisions at the edge of the frame in 2001: China's entry into the WTO, Beijing's winning bid for the 2008 Olympics. The teenagers in the foreground have nothing to do all day.
unknown-pleasures-2002.prism: The national good news plays at the edge of every shot and never reaches the people standing in it. That gap is the whole subject, and the documentary method is what makes it impossible to argue with.

turtles-can-fly-2004.gazette: Ghobadi cast local Kurdish children on the Iraq–Turkey border, among them refugees and kids maimed by landmines. The trade the film shows — digging mines out of the ground and selling them on — was ordinary work in that borderland, not invention. The injuries did not have to be designed by anyone.

colossal-youth-2006.gazette: Fontainhas, a Lisbon neighborhood built by Cape Verdean immigrants, was being demolished while Costa filmed its residents there as themselves. Ventura, who came to Portugal for construction work, carries the film under his own name, moving between the last standing rooms and the white rehousing blocks. The camera is set down and left there; nothing is restaged for it.

weekend-2011.gazette: Haigh shot in Nottingham with a small crew, in a real tower-block flat, letting scenes run long on a handheld camera. The two men talk the way people talk when no recorder is visible — overlapping, retracting, changing the subject. Two days, one flat, and no scene that announces itself as the important one.
weekend-2011.prism: Realism here is a limit on scale, not just a look: the film gets only what a weekend can hold. Everything that would usually be a third act happens off-screen, later, to people the camera doesn't follow.

the-bling-ring-2013.gazette: Between 2008 and 2009, a group of Los Angeles teenagers walked into the homes of Paris Hilton, Lindsay Lohan and other celebrities and carried out clothes, watches and cash, often through unlocked doors. Nancy Jo Sales reported the case for Vanity Fair, and Coppola built the film on that reporting, shooting in the Hollywood Hills where it happened. Hilton let the production film inside her actual house.

masaan-2015.gazette: Varanasi's burning ghats are an industry, staffed by hereditary labor held at the bottom of the caste order. Ghaywan filmed in that city and built the story out of it: a young man from the cremation trade, a young woman under police pressure, no villains anywhere. The river runs through both plots and registers neither.

capernaum-2018.gazette: Labaki cast the film out of Beirut's poorest streets; the boy at its center was a Syrian refugee living there, and the others stood close to the lives they play. The shoot ran long and loose, following children through real neighborhoods rather than sets. The court case the film is built around is a fiction, and almost nothing surrounding it is.
capernaum-2018.prism: Casting people to perform their own circumstances buys an authenticity nothing else can, and they are the ones who pay for it. The camera leaves; the neighborhood stays exactly where it was.

red-rocket-2021.gazette: Texas City is a refinery town, and Baker shot there in the summer of 2020 with a crew small enough not to close it down. Most of the faces around the lead were found locally and had never acted before. The refinery in the background is running; the film simply pointed at it.

no-bears-2022.gazette: Panahi, barred from making films in Iran, plays a director working from a village near the Turkish border, running a shoot he cannot legally attend. The border in the film is a real border, and the crossing it circles is the kind people were making at the time. He was arrested in July 2022; the film premiered in Venice that September without him.

vermiglio-2024.gazette: Delpero named the film after Vermiglio, an actual village in the Trentino Alps, and shot there in the local dialect. The story sits in the last winter of the Second World War, when the war reached that valley mainly as absent men and arriving strangers. Chores, seasons and Mass set the pace; the history arrives as weather.
vermiglio-2024.prism: Naming a real village makes the film answerable to it — the dialect, the shape of the year, what a household actually did in February. That's a heavier obligation than period costume, and the film takes it on.
